nodes.label: bun install --frozen-lockfile as a dependency coherence gate across CI and deploy scripts
nodes.norm_label: bun install --frozen-lockfile as a dependency coherence gate across ci and deploy scripts
nodes.summary: Reused id. Dependabot PR #438 edited four package.json manifests and left bun.lock untouched, so the gate fires: every one of the 13 `bun install --frozen-lockfile` call sites fails with "lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen". Merging shipped the P1 onto main.

nodes.label: Dependabot declared for npm while the repo resolves with Bun
nodes.norm_label: dependabot declared for npm while the repo resolves with bun
nodes.summary: Root cause of the blocker: `.github/dependabot.yml:3` declares `package-ecosystem: "npm"` although the repo installs and resolves with Bun. Dependabot's npm updater therefore rewrites manifests it does not understand well enough to lock, producing half-applied PRs. Switching the ecosystem value was the accepted fix.

nodes.label: Dependabot supports bun as a package-ecosystem value, version updates only
nodes.norm_label: dependabot supports bun as a package-ecosystem value, version updates only
nodes.summary: Verified against the GitHub docs rather than memory before editing the config: `bun` is a valid package-ecosystem YAML value, GA since 2025-02-13, requires Bun >= 1.1.39 (repo is on 1.4.0), covers the text bun.lock but not the legacy binary bun.lockb, and has no security-updates support yet.

nodes.label: Every @vitest/coverage-* release pins vitest to the identical exact version
nodes.norm_label: every @vitest/coverage-* release pins vitest to the identical exact version
nodes.summary: Checked against the npm registry before moving anything: coverage-istanbul 5.0.1 peer-pins vitest 5.0.1, coverage 5.0.3 peer-pins vitest 5.0.3. Provider and runner therefore cannot move independently, which is what finding F2 was about after Dependabot bumped the providers but not the runner.

nodes.label: Nested node_modules keeps the correct workerd binary while downloading a duplicate
nodes.norm_label: nested node_modules keeps the correct workerd binary while downloading a duplicate
nodes.summary: Reused id. The predicted duplicate stopped being a prediction: after regenerating the lock, node_modules holds 1.20260919.1 at the root (127 MB) and 1.20260911.1 nested under workerd (149 MB), about 276 MB of twin binary. Not a correctness break - wrangler and miniflare load the nested copy - and left unfixed as out of scope.

nodes.label: Root workerd-linux-64 pin is inert: no script or test imports it
nodes.norm_label: root workerd-linux-64 pin is inert: no script or test imports it
nodes.summary: Reused id. The root optionalDependencies pin buys nothing that the nested resolution does not already provide, so removing it or bumping workerd/wrangler together is the clean fix. Deliberately not touched: it sits outside the scope the user approved.

nodes.label: Stale # v6 and # ratchet annotations left behind by a SHA pin bump
nodes.norm_label: stale # v6 and # ratchet annotations left behind by a sha pin bump
nodes.summary: Finding F4 on PR #439, filed P2: three lines moved to the SHA 3d3c42e5..., verified via the GitHub API as the commit behind tag v7.0.1, while the trailing `# v6` comment and the `# ratchet:actions/checkout@v6` marker stayed at the old version.

nodes.label: Five red checks are billing cancellations, not build failures
nodes.norm_label: five red checks are billing cancellations, not build failures
nodes.summary: The five red checks on PR #438 came back "The job was not started because recent account payments have failed", every job with steps_count 0 and a 3-second duration. PR #439 reported no checks at all. Both still fail the auto-merge gates, but not for the reason the red X implies.

nodes.label: An EDQUOT from the reviewer's own probe directories is not a repo defect
nodes.norm_label: an edquot from the reviewer's own probe directories is not a repo defect
nodes.summary: The first CI simulation exited on EDQUOT because /tmp tmpfs was 80% full with the reviewer's own probe trees (1.4G plus 807M). Cleaning them up and re-running produced exit 0 on the exact pushed HEAD, so the failure belonged to the method, not the lockfile.

nodes.label: An already-merged PR is terminal: record the discrepancy, never revert
nodes.norm_label: an already-merged pr is terminal: record the discrepancy, never revert
nodes.summary: The user merged both PRs, including #438 which carried a P1. The response was to record the merge commits, re-verify the finding against the merged origin/main tree, and change nothing else: no revert, no un-merge, nothing posted.

nodes.label: schema-cli-fingerprint.yml exists only in the local working tree
nodes.norm_label: schema-cli-fingerprint.yml exists only in the local working tree
nodes.summary: The file is untracked and absent from origin/main, which is why PR #439 left it on actions/checkout@v4 at line 58. Recorded explicitly as local repo state and out of scope for the PR, since Dependabot only ever reads the tracked base.

nodes.label: Align vitest to the already-merged coverage version rather than to latest
nodes.norm_label: align vitest to the already-merged coverage version rather than to latest
nodes.summary: Coverage is exact-pinned in this repo and PR #438 already merged 5.0.1, so resolving the lock to vitest 5.0.1 is the only self-consistent pairing that adds no version drift beyond what is already on main. Going to 5.0.3 would re-pin the providers into an unreviewed bump.

nodes.label: Re-verify the blocker against the merged origin/main tree, not the synthetic probe
nodes.norm_label: re-verify the blocker against the merged origin main tree, not the synthetic probe
nodes.summary: The first reproduction used a hand-built workspace. After the merge the claim was re-checked with `git archive origin/main package.json bun.lock patches apps config` piped into `bun install --frozen-lockfile`: exit 1, lockfile frozen. Evidence from the real tree beats evidence from the model of it.

nodes.label: P1 rather than P0 because no workflow is actually running
nodes.norm_label: p1 rather than p0 because no workflow is actually running
nodes.summary: P0 would need universal failure independent of inputs. The frozen-lockfile contract is documented and spans 13 install sites, which is P1, but ci.yml is workflow_dispatch-only and Actions are disabled, so nothing is breaking live. Severity was lowered on that basis, not on convenience; the verdict stayed `not correct` either way.

nodes.label: The coverage/vitest peer mismatch only warns in bun, so it is P2 not blocking
nodes.norm_label: the coverage/vitest peer mismatch only warns in bun, so it is p2 not blocking
nodes.summary: A reviewer subagent called the peer conflict a confirmed risk case. A parent-side probe showed a non-frozen install prints `incorrect peer dependency` and exits 0, which contradicts the subagent, so the finding was downgraded rather than passed on.

nodes.label: The wrangler SHA-pin finding was dropped because no such convention exists
nodes.norm_label: the wrangler sha-pin finding was dropped because no such convention exists
nodes.summary: A reviewer flagged that moving wrangler-action to @v4.1.3 breaks a SHA-pin convention. The repo overwhelmingly uses floating tags (checkout@v7, setup-bun@v2, rust-cache@v2, gitleaks@v3) and the three SHA-pinned workflows are the exception, so the claim failed the deliberate-design-choice criterion and was recorded as rejected.

nodes.label: Zero steps and a 3-second duration mark a job that never started
nodes.norm_label: zero steps and a 3-second duration mark a job that never started
nodes.summary: No step can fail in under three seconds with an empty steps array, so the red X was a job that was never allocated a runner. That reading is what separated an account billing artefact from a repository breakage, and it was confirmed independently against the API rather than taken from the subagent.

nodes.label: Switching npm to bun loses nothing because no security-updates block exists
nodes.norm_label: switching npm to bun loses nothing because no security-updates block exists
nodes.summary: Bun security updates are not supported by Dependabot yet, which looked like a regression until the config was re-read: it declares only npm, cargo and github-actions version updates and no security-updates section, so the gap applies to nothing that was configured.

nodes.label: No revert, because a revert is a new change and not an undo
nodes.norm_label: no revert, because a revert is a new change and not an undo
nodes.summary: The P1 finding was correct and the PR was merged anyway, which is the user's call. The chosen response was to verify and write down the consequence, not to undo the merge - merged is terminal, and un-merging would substitute an agent decision for a human one.
